title: On the Weak Right Order of a Right-Angled Coxeter System
summary: Let $ (W,S)$ be a Coxeter system, and let $ w\in W$. Let $ [1,w] := \{ x\in W \mid x \leq_{R} w \} $ where $ \leq_{R}$ denotes the weak right order of $ (W,S)$. The element $ w$ is said to have the \emph{ancestor property} if there is a unique non-trivial involution of maximal length in the set $ [1,w]$. The ancestor property was first defined by Hart and Rowley in \cite{hart2025noteinvolutionprefixescoxeter} where they conjectured that all non-identity elements in a finite Coxeter system have the ancestor property.
